Subpart A—General
§ 851.101
Scope.
(a) This part implements Title VIII of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended (
50 U.S.C. 4581-4589
) (Title VIII), which directs the Secretary of the Treasury (the Secretary), in consultation with the Secretary of Commerce, the Secretary of State, and, as appropriate, the heads of other relevant Federal departments and agencies (as defined in § 851.229), to issue, subject to public notice and comment, regulations to require a U.S. person to provide written notification on behalf of itself or its controlled foreign entity regarding certain covered national security transactions in any notifiable technology and, where the Secretary has exercised the authority under Title VIII to prohibit certain transactions, to prohibit a U.S. person and its controlled foreign entities from engaging in certain covered national security transactions in any prohibited technology.
(b) This part identifies certain types of transactions that are
covered national security transactions
—which are certain transactions by a
U.S. person
into or with a
covered foreign person.
Additionally, this part identifies other instances where a
U.S. person
has obligations with respect to certain transactions. The regulations prescribe exceptions to the definition of
covered national security transaction.
A transaction that meets an exception is not a
covered national security transaction
and is referred to as an
excepted transaction.
Finally, this part:
(1) Exempts any authorized intelligence activities of the United States; and
(2) Prescribes a process to consider exempting certain activities from the definition of a
covered national security transaction
on a case-by-case basis.
(c) This part identifies categories of
covered national security transactions
that are
notifiable transactions.
A
notifiable transaction
is a
covered national security transaction
by a
U.S. person
or its
controlled foreign entity
with a
covered foreign person
or a relevant joint venture involving a
notifiable technology.
A
notifiable transaction
includes a
U.S. person'
s direction of a transaction that the
U.S. person
knows would be a
notifiable transaction
if engaged in by a
U.S. person
(other than an acquisition of a limited partner interest or equivalent in a pooled investment fund that is not a
U.S. person
). This part requires a
U.S. person
to notify the Department of the Treasury of each such
notifiable transaction
by such
U.S. person
or its
controlled foreign entity.
This part also requires a
U.S. person
to provide prompt notice to the Department of the Treasury upon acquiring actual knowledge after the
completion date
of a transaction of facts or circumstances that would have caused the transaction to be a
covered national security transaction
if the
U.S. person
had such knowledge on the
completion date.
Additionally, any person who makes a representation, statement, or certification to the Department of the Treasury under this part is required to promptly notify the Department of the Treasury upon learning of a material omission or inaccuracy in such representation, statement, or certification.
(d) This part identifies categories of
covered national security transactions
that are
prohibited transactions.
A
prohibited transaction
is a
covered national security transaction
by a
U.S. person
with a
covered foreign person
or relevant joint venture involving a
prohibited technology.
This part prohibits a
U.S. person
from knowingly engaging in a
prohibited transaction,
which includes a prohibition on a
U.S. person'
s direction of a transaction that the
U.S. person
knows would be a
prohibited transaction
if engaged in by a
U.S. person
(other than an acquisition of a limited partner interest or equivalent in a pooled investment fund that is not a
U.S. person
). This part also requires a
U.S. person
to take all reasonable steps to prohibit and prevent any transaction by its
controlled foreign entity
that would be a
prohibited transaction
if undertaken by a
U.S. person.
(e) This part provides for the imposition of civil penalties for any violation, and the Secretary has the authority to compel divestment of a
covered national security transaction
in a
prohibited technology.
Pursuant to Title VIII, the Secretary also is required to establish a process to identify
covered national security transactions
for which no notification was submitted and for which information is reasonably available.
(f) The Secretary should, as appropriate:
(1) Coordinate with the Secretary of Commerce, the Secretary of State, and the heads of other relevant Federal departments and agencies, to determine whether certain activity is in the national interest of the United States and should be exempted from prohibition;
(2) Consult with the Secretary of Commerce, the Secretary of State, and,
(
printed page 67420)
as appropriate, the heads of other relevant Federal departments and agencies, when issuing or updating regulations to implement Title VIII;
(3) Consult with the Secretary of Commerce and, as appropriate, the heads of other relevant Federal departments and agencies, regarding the report required by section 803 of Title VIII;
(4) Consult with the Secretary of Commerce regarding the establishment of a publicly accessible, non-exhaustive database that identifies covered foreign persons that are either engaged in a prohibited technology or a notifiable technology and a mechanism for a covered foreign person to petition for removal or inclusion in such a database; and
(5) Coordinate with the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Commerce, and the heads of other relevant Federal departments and agencies to:
(i) Conduct bilateral and multilateral engagement with allies and partners to promote and increase coordination of protocols and procedures to facilitate the effective implementation of and appropriate compliance with the prohibition and notification requirement pursuant to Title VIII;
(ii) Work with allies and partners to establish mechanisms for information sharing; and
(iii) Work with and encourage allies and partners to develop outbound investment screening mechanisms to prevent the development of prohibited technologies by countries of concern.
§ 851.102
Relation of this part to other laws and regulations.
(a) Nothing in this part may be construed to alter, affect, or negate any other authority, process, regulation, investigation, enforcement measure, license, authorization, or review provided by or established under any other provision of Federal law, including the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) (
50 U.S.C. 1701
et seq.
), or any other authority of the President or the Congress under the Constitution of the United States. This part is separate from, and independent of, the other parts of this subtitle. Differing foreign policy and national security circumstances may result in differing interpretations of the same or similar language among the separate parts of this subtitle. No action taken pursuant to any other provision of law or regulation, including the other parts of this subtitle, authorizes any transaction prohibited by this part or alters any other obligation under this part. No action taken pursuant to this part relieves any party from complying with any other applicable laws or regulations.
(b) The regulations in this part apply from [EFFECTIVE DATE OF FINAL RULE].
(c) For any activities of a U.S. person to which part 850 of this chapter was applicable on or after January 2, 2025, and prior to [EFFECTIVE DATE OF FINAL RULE], the regulations in part 850 of this chapter will continue to apply.
§ 851.103
Rules of construction and interpretation.
(a) As used in this part, the term “including” (or variations such as “include”) means “including but not limited to.”
(b) Any term in the singular includes the plural, and the plural includes the singular, if such use would be appropriate.
(c) Section headings are included for convenience of reference only and shall not affect the interpretation of this part.
§ 851.104
Knowledge standard.
(a) Certain provisions of this part apply only if a U.S. person
knows
of a fact or circumstance. The term
knowledge
is defined in § 851.217. In determining whether a U.S. person is complying with this part or has violated any obligation under this part, the Department of the Treasury will assess whether such person has or had knowledge of the relevant facts and circumstances at the specified time.
(b) Such assessment as to whether, at the time of a given transaction, a U.S. person has or had knowledge of a given fact or circumstance will be made based on information a U.S. person had or could have had through a reasonable and diligent inquiry. A U.S. person that has failed to conduct a reasonable and diligent inquiry by the time of a given transaction may be assessed to have had reason to know of a given fact or circumstance, including facts or circumstances that would cause the transaction to be a covered national security transaction in a notifiable technology or a prohibited technology.
(c) In assessing whether a U.S. person has undertaken such a reasonable and diligent inquiry, the Department of the Treasury's considerations will include the following, as applicable, among others that the Department of the Treasury deems relevant, with respect to a particular transaction:
(1) The inquiry a U.S. person has made regarding an investment target or other relevant party, including questions asked of the investment target or relevant party, as of the time of the transaction;
(2) The contractual representations or warranties the U.S. person has obtained or attempted to obtain from the investment target or other relevant party with respect to the determination of a transaction's status as a covered national security transaction in a notifiable technology or a prohibited technology and the status of an investment target or other relevant party as a covered foreign person;
(3) The efforts by the U.S. person as of the time of the transaction to obtain and consider available non-public information relevant to the determination of a transaction's status as a covered national security transaction in a notifiable technology or prohibited technology and the status of an investment target or other relevant party as a covered foreign person;
(4) Available public information, the efforts undertaken by the U.S. person to obtain and consider such information, and the degree to which other information available to the U.S. person as of the time of the transaction is consistent or inconsistent with such publicly available information;
(5) Whether the U.S. person purposefully avoided learning or seeking relevant information;
(6) The presence or absence of warning signs, which may include evasive responses or non-responses from an investment target or other relevant party to questions or a refusal to provide information, contractual representations, or warranties;
(7) The use of available public and commercial databases to identify and verify relevant information of an investment target or other relevant party; and
(8) Whether the U.S. person appropriately considered any information made available by the Department of the Treasury prior to the completion of the transaction, including any assessments by the Department of the Treasury that the relevant covered foreign person may be engaged in a notifiable technology or a prohibited technology.
(d) An assessment of whether a U.S. person has undertaken a reasonable and diligent inquiry shall be based on a consideration of the totality of relevant facts and circumstances.
(e) Paragraphs (a) through (d) of this section shall also apply to the
knowledge
of a controlled foreign entity for the purposes of applying §§ 851.402 and 851.403.

Subpart B—Definitions
§ 851.201
Advanced packaging.
The term
advanced packaging
means to package integrated circuits in a manner that supports the two-and-one-half-dimensional (2.5D) or three-dimensional (3D) assembly of integrated circuits, such as by directly attaching one or more die or wafer using through-silicon vias, die or wafer bonding, heterogeneous integration, or other advanced methods and materials.
§ 851.202
Affiliate.
The term
affiliate
means, in the context of a transaction or activity covered under this part, a person that directly, or indirectly through one or more intermediaries, controls or is controlled by, or is under common control with, a person subject to this part.
§ 851.203
Certification.
(a) The term
certification
means a written statement signed by the chief executive officer or other duly authorized designee of the person filing a notification or providing other information that certifies under the penalties provided in the False Statements Accountability Act of 1996, as amended (
18 U.S.C. 1001
), that the notification or other information filed or provided:
(1) Fully complies with the regulations in this part; and
(2) Is accurate and complete in all material respects to the best knowledge of the person filing a notification or other information.
(b) For purposes of this section, a duly authorized designee is:
(1) In the case of a partnership, any general partner thereof;
(2) In the case of a corporation, any officer thereof; and
(3) In the case of any entity lacking partners and officers, any individual within the organization exercising executive functions similar to those of a general partner of a partnership or an officer of a corporation or otherwise authorized by the board of directors or equivalent to provide such certification.
(c) In each case described in paragraph (b) of this section, such designee must possess actual authority to make the certification on behalf of the person filing a notification or other information.
Note 1 to § 851.203:
A template for certifications may be found at the Department of the Treasury's Outbound Investment Security Program website.
§ 851.204
Completion date.
The term
completion date
means:
(a) With respect to a covered national security transaction other than under § 851.209(a)(7), the earliest date upon which any interest, asset, property, or right is conveyed, assigned, delivered, or otherwise transferred to a U.S. person, or as applicable, its controlled foreign entity; or
(b) With respect to a covered national security transaction under § 851.209(a)(7), the earliest date upon which any interest, asset, property, or right in the relevant covered foreign person is conveyed, assigned, delivered, or otherwise transferred to the applicable fund.
§ 851.205
Contingent equity interest.
The term
contingent equity interest
means a financial interest (including debt) that currently does not constitute an equity interest but is convertible into, or provides the right to acquire, an equity interest upon the occurrence of a contingency or defined event or at the discretion of the U.S. person that holds the financial interest.
§ 851.206
Controlled foreign entity.
(a) The term
controlled foreign entity
means any entity incorporated in, or otherwise organized under the laws of, a country other than the United States of which a U.S. person is a parent.
(b) For purposes of the term
controlled foreign entity,
the following rules shall apply in determining whether an entity is a parent of another entity in a tiered ownership structure:
(1) Where the relationship between an entity and another entity is that of parent and subsidiary, the holdings of voting interest or voting power of the board, as applicable, of a subsidiary shall be fully attributed to the parent.
(2) Where the relationship between an entity and another entity is not that of parent and subsidiary (
i.e.,
because the holdings of voting interest or voting power of the board, as applicable, of the first entity in the second entity is 50 percent or less), then the indirect downstream holdings of voting interest or voting power of the board, as applicable, attributed to the first entity shall be determined proportionately.
(3) Where the circumstances in paragraphs (b)(1) and (2) of this section apply (
i.e.,
because a U.S. person holds both direct and indirect downstream holdings in the same entity), any holdings of voting interest shall be aggregated for the purposes of applying the definition in this section, and any holdings of voting power of the board shall be aggregated for the purposes of applying the definition in this section. Voting interest shall not be aggregated with voting power of the board for the purposes of applying the definition in this section.
§ 851.207
Country of concern.
The term
country of concern
means any of the following:
(a) The People's Republic of China, including the Hong Kong and Macau Special Administrative Regions;
(b) The Republic of Cuba;
(c) The Islamic Republic of Iran;
(d) The Democratic People's Republic of Korea;
(e) The Russian Federation; and
(f) The Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela under the regime of Nicolás Maduro Moros.
§ 851.208
Covered foreign person.
(a) The term
covered foreign person
means a foreign person that:
(1) Is an individual that:
(i) Is a citizen or permanent resident of a country of concern;
(ii) Is not a U.S. citizen; and
(iii) Is not a permanent resident of the United States;
(2) Is an entity incorporated in, has a principal place of business in, or is otherwise organized under the laws of a country of concern;
(3) Is an individual that is a member of the Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party or is otherwise a member of the political leadership of a country of concern;
(4) Is the government of a country of concern, including any political subdivision, political party, agency, or instrumentality thereof, or any person acting for or on behalf of the government of a country of concern;
(5) Is an entity owned in the aggregate, directly or indirectly, 50 percent or more, in terms of outstanding voting interest, voting power of the board, or equity interest, by a foreign person meeting the criteria of paragraphs (a)(1) through (4) of this section;
(6) Is an entity directly or indirectly subject to the direction or control of a foreign person meeting the criteria of paragraphs (a)(1) through (4) of this section;
(7) Is an entity in which one or more foreign persons meeting the criteria of paragraph (a)(5) or (6) of this section, individually or in the aggregate, directly or indirectly, holds at least 50 percent of any of the following interests of such entity: outstanding voting interest, voting power of the board, or equity interest; or
(8) Is an entity that directly or indirectly holds a board seat on, a voting or equity interest (other than through securities or interests that would satisfy the conditions in
(
printed page 67422)
§ 851.501(a) if held by a U.S. person) in, or any contractual power to direct or cause the direction of the management or policies of any person or persons meeting the criteria of paragraphs (a)(1) through (7) of this section that engage(s) in a notifiable technology or prohibited technology and from or through which it:
(i) Derives more than 50 percent of its revenue individually, or as aggregated across such persons from each of which it derives at least $50,000 (or equivalent) of its revenue, on an annual basis;
(ii) Derives more than 50 percent of its net income individually, or as aggregated across such persons from each of which it derives at least $50,000 (or equivalent) of its net income, on an annual basis;
(iii) Incurs more than 50 percent of its capital expenditure individually, or as aggregated across such persons from each of which it incurs at least $50,000 (or equivalent) of its capital expenditure, on an annual basis; or
(iv) Incurs more than 50 percent of its operating expenses individually, or as aggregated across such persons from each of which it incurs at least $50,000 (or equivalent) of its operating expenses, on an annual basis.
(b) As used in paragraph (a)(6) of this section,
subject to the direction or control
means that the government of a country of concern (including any political subdivision, political party, agency, or instrumentality thereof, or any person acting for or on behalf of the government of a country of concern), the individual described in paragraph (a)(1) or (3) of this section, or entity described in paragraph (a)(2) of this section has the power, directly or indirectly, to direct or cause the direction of the management or policies of such entity (whether through the ownership of voting securities, by contract, or otherwise).
(c) For purposes of paragraph (a)(8) of this section:
(1) Calculations shall be based on an audited financial statement from the most recent year. If an audited financial statement is not available, the most recent unaudited financial statement shall be used instead. If no financial statement is available, an independent appraisal shall be used instead. If no independent appraisal is available, a good-faith estimate shall be used instead.
(2) Where an amount is not denominated in U.S. dollars, the U.S. dollar equivalent shall be determined based on the most recent published rate of exchange available on the Department of the Treasury's website.
(d) References in paragraph (a)(8) of this section to revenue, net income, capital expenditure, or operating expenses refer to overall revenue, net income, capital expenditure, or operating expenses, as applicable, without subtracting amounts attributable to persons described in paragraph (a) of this section of less than $50,000 (or equivalent).
§ 851.209
Covered national security transaction.
(a) The term
covered national security transaction
means a U.S. person's direct or indirect:
(1) Acquisition of an equity interest or contingent equity interest in a covered foreign person that the U.S. person knows at the time of the acquisition is a covered foreign person that engages in a notifiable technology or a prohibited technology or that meets the conditions set forth under § 851.208(a)(8);
(2) Provision of a loan or a similar debt financing arrangement to a covered foreign person that the U.S. person knows at the time of the provision is a covered foreign person that engages in a notifiable technology or a prohibited technology or that meets the conditions set forth under § 851.208(a)(8), where such debt financing affords or will afford the U.S. person an interest in profits of the covered foreign person, the right to appoint members of the board of directors (or equivalent) of the covered foreign person, or other comparable financial or governance rights characteristic of an equity investment but not typical of a loan;
provided:
(i) Neither the issuance of a secured loan or similar debt financing for which equity is pledged as collateral, nor the acquisition of such secured debt on the secondary market, is an acquisition of an equity interest; and
(ii) Foreclosure on collateral where the debtholder takes possession of the pledged equity is an acquisition of an equity interest;
provided that
such an acquisition is not a covered national security transaction where the equity was pledged prior to [EFFECTIVE DATE OF FINAL RULE], or where the U.S. person did not know at the time of issuing or acquiring the debt that the pledged equity was in a covered foreign person that engages in a notifiable technology or prohibited technology;
(3) Entrance into a joint venture, wherever located, that is formed with a covered foreign person, and that the U.S. person knows at the time of entrance into the joint venture that the joint venture will engage, or plans to engage, in a notifiable technology or a prohibited technology;
(4) Conversion of a contingent equity interest (or interest equivalent to a contingent equity interest) or conversion of debt to an equity interest in a covered foreign person that the U.S. person knows at the time of the conversion is a covered foreign person that engages in a notifiable technology or prohibited technology or that meets the conditions set forth under § 851.208(a)(8), where the contingent equity interest (or equivalent) or debt was acquired by the U.S. person on or after [EFFECTIVE DATE OF FINAL RULE];
(5) Acquisition, leasing, or other development of operations, land, property, or other assets in a country of concern that the U.S. person knows at the time of such acquisition, leasing, or other development will result in, or that the U.S. person plans to result in:
(i) The establishment of a covered foreign person that engages in a notifiable technology or prohibited technology; or
(ii) The engagement of a covered foreign person in a prohibited technology or notifiable technology;
(6) Direction of a transaction by a foreign person that the U.S. person knows at the time of the transaction would constitute a transaction described in paragraph (a)(1), (2), (3), (4), or (5) of this section, if engaged in by a U.S. person;
provided:
(i) The U.S. person has authority, individually or as part of a group, to make or substantially participate in decisions on behalf of a foreign person (including being an officer or director of, or otherwise possessing executive responsibilities with respect to, the foreign person) and, individually or as part of a group, exercises that authority to, direct, order, decide upon, or approve a transaction that the U.S. person knows would be a covered national security transaction if engaged in by a U.S. person.
(ii) A U.S. person that recuses from the following activities will not be considered to have directed a covered national security transaction under this paragraph (a)(6):
(A) Participating in approval and decision-making processes related to the transaction, including making a recommendation;
(B) Reviewing, editing, commenting on, approving, and signing relevant transaction documents; and
(C) Engaging in negotiations with the investment target (or, as applicable, the relevant transaction counterparty, such as a joint venture partner); or
(7) Acquisition of a limited partner or equivalent interest in a venture capital fund, private equity fund, fund of funds, or other pooled investment fund (in
(
printed page 67423)
each case where the fund is not a U.S. person) that the U.S. person knows at the time of the acquisition likely will invest in a covered foreign person that is in the semiconductor technology and microelectronics, super intelligence systems, quantum information technologies, hypersonic systems, high-performance computing and supercomputing, or biotechnology sectors, and such fund undertakes a transaction that would be a covered national security transaction if undertaken by a U.S. person.
(b) Notwithstanding paragraph (a) of this section, a transaction is not a covered national security transaction if it is an excepted transaction as set forth in § 851.501.
(c) The acquisition of a contingent interest described in paragraph (a)(1) of this section may constitute a covered national security transaction, and the subsequent occurrence of a conversion event described in paragraph (a)(4) of this section may constitute a separate covered national security transaction. A U.S. person should assess each of the acquisition and the conversion to determine the applicability of this part.
(d) An indirect covered national security transaction in a notifiable technology or prohibited technology includes a U.S. person's use of an intermediary to engage in a transaction that would be a covered national security transaction if engaged in directly by a U.S. person.
(e) For purposes of paragraph (a)(1) of this section, a U.S. person is not considered to have acquired an indirect equity interest or contingent equity interest in a covered foreign person when the U.S. person acquires a limited partner or equivalent interest in a venture capital fund, private equity fund, fund of funds, or other pooled investment fund and that fund then acquires an equity interest or contingent equity interest in a covered foreign person. (A U.S. person's acquisition of a limited partner or equivalent interest in a non-U.S. person venture capital fund, private equity fund, fund of funds, or other pooled investment fund may, however, be a covered national security transaction under paragraph (a)(7) of this section.)
§ 851.210

§ 851.211
Entity.

Subpart C—Prohibited Transactions and Other Prohibited Activities
§ 851.301
Undertaking a prohibited transaction.
A U.S. person may not engage in a prohibited transaction unless an exemption for that transaction has been granted under § 851.502 or the transaction qualifies for the exemption under § 851.503.
§ 851.302
Actions of a controlled foreign entity.
(a) A U.S. person shall take all reasonable steps to prohibit and prevent any transaction by its controlled foreign entity that would be a prohibited transaction if engaged in by a U.S. person.
(b) If a controlled foreign entity engages in a transaction that would be a prohibited transaction if engaged in by a U.S. person, in determining whether the relevant U.S. person took all reasonable steps to prohibit and prevent such transaction, the Department of the Treasury will consider, among other factors, any of the following with respect to a U.S. person and its controlled foreign entity:
(1) The execution of agreements with respect to compliance with the regulations in this part between the subject U.S. person and its controlled foreign entity;
(2) The existence and exercise of governance or shareholder rights by the U.S. person with respect to the controlled foreign entity, where applicable;
(3) The existence and implementation of periodic training and internal reporting requirements by the U.S. person and its controlled foreign entity with respect to compliance with the regulations in this part;
(4) The implementation of appropriate and documented internal controls, including internal policies, procedures, or guidelines that are periodically reviewed internally, by the U.S. person and its controlled foreign entity; and
(5) Implementation of a documented testing and/or auditing process of internal controls, policies, procedures, or guidelines.
Note 1 to § 851.302:
Findings of violations of this section and decisions related to enforcement and penalties will be made based on a consideration of the totality of relevant facts and circumstances, including whether the U.S. person has taken the steps described in paragraph (b) of this section and whether such steps were reasonable in light of the relevant facts and circumstances.
Subpart D—Notifiable Transactions and Other Notifiable Activities
§ 851.401
Undertaking a notifiable transaction.
A U.S. person that engages in a notifiable transaction shall file a notification of that transaction with the Department of the Treasury pursuant to § 851.404.
§ 851.402
Notification of actions of a controlled foreign entity.
A U.S. person shall file a notification with the Department of the Treasury pursuant to § 851.404 with respect to any transaction undertaken by a controlled foreign entity of the U.S. person that the controlled foreign entity or the U.S. person knew at the time of the transaction would be a notifiable transaction if engaged in by a U.S. person.
§ 851.403
Notification of post-transaction knowledge.
If a U.S. person or its controlled foreign entity acquires actual knowledge after the completion date of a transaction of a fact or circumstance such that the transaction would have been a notifiable transaction or prohibited transaction if such knowledge had been possessed by the relevant U.S. person at the time of the transaction, then the relevant U.S. person shall promptly, and in no event later than 30 calendar days following the acquisition of such knowledge, submit a notification pursuant to § 851.404.

Note 1 to § 851.403:

§ 851.404
Procedures for notifications.
(a) A U.S. person that has an obligation under § 851.401, § 851.402, or § 851.403 shall file an electronic copy of the notification of the transaction with the Department of the Treasury including the information set out in § 851.405 and a certification referred to in § 851.203. The U.S. person shall follow the electronic filing instructions posted on the Department of the Treasury's Outbound Investment Security Program website. No communications or submissions other than those described in this section shall constitute the filing of a notification for purposes of this part.
(b) The Department of the Treasury may contact a U.S. person that has filed a notification with questions or document requests (including questions or document requests made on behalf of other relevant Federal departments or agencies) related to the transaction or compliance with the regulations in this part. The U.S. person shall respond to any such questions or requests within the time frame and in the manner specified by the Department of the Treasury. Information and other documents provided by the U.S. person to the Department of the Treasury after the filing of the notification under this section shall be deemed part of the notification and shall be subject to the certification set out in § 851.203.
(c) A U.S. person shall file a notification under § 851.401 or § 851.402 with the Department of the Treasury no later than 30 calendar days following the completion date of a notifiable transaction. A U.S. person shall file a notification required under § 851.403 with the Department of the Treasury no later than 30 calendar days after it acquires the knowledge referred to in § 851.403.
(d) If a U.S. person files a notification prior to the completion date of the notifiable transaction, the U.S. person shall update such notification no later than 30 calendar days following the completion date of the notifiable transaction if information in the original filing has materially changed.
(e) A U.S. person shall inform the Department of the Treasury in writing no later than 30 calendar days following the acquisition of previously unavailable information required under § 851.405.

Such supporting documentation shall include, as applicable, any pitch decks, marketing letters, and offering memorandums; transaction documents including side letters and investment agreements; and due diligence materials related to the transaction. (d) If the U.S. person does not provide responses to the information required in paragraph (b) of this section, the U.S. person shall provide sufficient explanation for why the information is unavailable or otherwise cannot be obtained and explain the U.S. person's efforts to obtain such information. If such information subsequently becomes available, the U.S. person shall provide such information to the Department of the Treasury promptly, and no later than 30 calendar days following the availability of such information.
§ 851.406
Notice of material omission or inaccuracy.
A person who has made any representation, statement, or certification subject to this part, including in connection with any enforcement inquiry or action pursuant to subpart F of this part, shall inform the Department of the Treasury in writing promptly, and in no event later than 30 calendar days after learning of a material omission or inaccuracy in such representation, statement, or certification.
Subpart E—Exceptions and Exemptions
§ 851.501
Excepted transaction.
A transaction that would be either a prohibited transaction or a notifiable transaction if engaged in by a U.S. person but for this section is not a prohibited transaction or a notifiable transaction, as applicable, if the conditions set forth in this section are met. In that case, the transaction is an excepted transaction. The following transactions are excepted transactions:
(a)(1) An investment by a U.S. person:
(i) In a “security” as defined in section 3(a)(10) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, at
15 U.S.C. 78c(a)(10)
, denominated in any currency, and that trades on an exchange or the over-the-counter market in any jurisdiction;
(ii) In a security issued by any “investment company” as defined in section 3(a)(1) of the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended, at
15 U.S.C. 80a-3(a)(1)
, that is registered with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, such as an index fund, mutual fund, or exchange traded fund;
(iii) In connection with a transaction described in § 851.209(a)(7), made as a limited partner or equivalent in a venture capital fund, private equity fund, fund of funds, or other pooled investment fund other than as described in paragraph (a)(1)(ii) of this section, where:
(A) The limited partner or equivalent's committed capital is not more than the
de minimis
amount of $2,000,000, aggregated across any investment and co-investment vehicles of the fund; or
(B) The limited partner or equivalent has secured a binding contractual assurance that its capital in the fund will not be used to engage in a transaction that would be a prohibited transaction or notifiable transaction, as applicable, if engaged in by a U.S. person; or
(iv) In a derivative of a security described under paragraph (a)(1)(i), (ii), or (iii) of this section; and
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (a)(1) of this section, an investment is not an excepted transaction if it affords the U.S. person governance rights beyond standard minority shareholder protections with respect to the covered foreign person. Such standard minority shareholder protections include:
(i) The power to prevent the sale or pledge of all or substantially all of the assets of an entity or a voluntary filing for bankruptcy or liquidation;
(ii) The power to prevent an entity from entering into contracts with majority investors or their affiliates;
(iii) The power to prevent an entity from guaranteeing the obligations of majority investors or their affiliates;
(iv) The right to purchase an additional interest in an entity to prevent the dilution of an investor's pro rata interest in that entity in the event that the entity issues additional instruments conveying interests in the entity;
(v) The power to prevent the change of existing legal rights or preferences of the particular class of stock held by minority investors, as provided in the relevant corporate documents governing such stock; and
(vi) The power to prevent the amendment of the Articles of Incorporation, constituent agreement, or other organizational documents of an entity with respect to the matters described in paragraphs (a)(2)(i) through (v) of this section;
(
printed page 67429)
(b) The acquisition by a U.S. person of equity or other interest owned or held by a covered foreign person in an entity or assets located outside of a country of concern in which the U.S. person is acquiring the totality of the equity or other interest in such entity held by all covered foreign persons and, following such acquisition, the entity does not constitute a covered foreign person;
(c) An intracompany transfer of funds (as defined in § 851.216) from a U.S. person to its controlled foreign entity;
(d) A transaction made on or after [EFFECTIVE DATE OF FINAL RULE] pursuant to a binding, uncalled capital commitment entered into before [EFFECTIVE DATE OF FINAL RULE];
(e) The acquisition of a voting interest in a covered foreign person by a U.S. person upon default or other condition involving a loan or a similar financing arrangement, where the loan was made by a syndicate of banks in a loan participation where the U.S. person lender(s) in the syndicate:
(1) Cannot on its own initiate any action vis-à-vis the debtor; and
(2) Is not the syndication agent;
(f) The receipt of employment compensation by an individual in the form of an award of equity or the grant of an option to purchase equity in a covered foreign person, or the exercise of such option;
(g) Transactions that would otherwise be notifiable transactions, where neither the value of the covered national security transaction, nor provision of funds or other consideration to the relevant covered foreign person or joint venture, in the aggregate across the preceding 12 months, exceeds the
de minimis
amount of $50,000 (When applying the
de minimis
exception, the U.S. person must account for any funds provided and the fair market value of any non-cash consideration. The Department of the Treasury is not bound by the U.S. person's valuation of the transaction or transactions.);
(h) A transaction secondary to a covered national security transaction,
i.e.:
(1) Contractual arrangements (not including contractual arrangements for technology transfer or technical knowledge transfer) or the procurement of material inputs for any covered national security transaction (such as raw materials);
(2) Bank lending;
(3) The processing, clearing, or sending of payments by a bank;
(4) Underwriting services including, but not limited to, the temporary acquisition of an equity interest for the sole purpose of facilitating underwriting services;
(5) Debt rating services;
(6) Prime brokerage;
(7) Global custody;
(8) Equity research or analysis; or
(9) Other similar services;
(i) Any ordinary or administrative business transaction;
(j) Any ancillary transaction undertaken by a “financial institution” as defined in
31 U.S.C. 5312
,
i.e.:
(1) The processing, clearing, or sending of payments and cash transactions for or to a covered foreign person;
(2) Underwriting services, including the temporary acquisition of an equity interest in a covered foreign person for the sole purpose of facilitating underwriting services;
(3) Credit rating services on behalf of a covered foreign person; and
(4) Other services ordinarily incident to and part of the provision of financial services on behalf of a covered foreign person, such as opening deposit accounts, direct custody services, foreign exchange services, remittances services, and safe deposit services;
(k)(1) A transaction that is:
(i) With or involving a person of a country or territory outside of the United States designated by the Secretary, after taking into account whether the country or territory is addressing national security risks substantially similar to those described in section 8504 of Subtitle A of Title LXXXV of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 and related to outbound investment; and
(ii) Of a type for which the Secretary has determined that the related national security concerns are likely to be adequately addressed by measures taken or that may be taken by the government of the relevant country or territory.
(2) Prior to making a designation or determination under this paragraph (k), the Secretary shall consult with the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Commerce, and, as appropriate, the heads of other relevant Federal departments and agencies.
(3) The Secretary's designations and determinations under paragraph (k)(1) of this section shall be made available through public notice.
(4) The Secretary may rescind a designation or determination under paragraph (k)(1) of this section if the Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of State, Secretary of Commerce, and, as appropriate, the heads of other relevant agencies, determines that such a rescission is appropriate. Any rescission shall be made available through public notice; or
(l) Any transaction completed before the enactment of Title VIII on December 18, 2025 (although transactions prior to this date may be subject to part 850 of this chapter).
§ 851.502
National interest exemption.
(a) The Secretary, in coordination with the Secretary of Commerce, the Secretary of State, and the heads of other relevant Federal departments and agencies, as appropriate, may determine that a covered national security transaction is in the national interest of the United States and therefore is exempt from applicable provisions in subpart C of this part (excluding §§ 851.406, 851.603, and 851.604). Such a determination may be made following a request by a U.S. person on its own behalf or on behalf of its controlled foreign entity.
(b) Any determination pursuant to paragraph (a) of this section will be based on a consideration of the totality of the relevant facts and circumstances and may be informed by, among other considerations, the transaction's effect on critical U.S. supply chain needs; domestic production needs in the United States for projected national defense requirements; U.S. public health needs; U.S. technological leadership globally in areas affecting U.S. national security; and impact on U.S. national security if the U.S. person is prohibited from undertaking the transaction.
(c) The Secretary shall:
(1) Notify the appropriate congressional committees not later than five business days after issuing an exemption under paragraph (a) of this section; and
(2) Include in such notification an identification of the national interest justifying the use of the exemption, subject to appropriate confidentiality and classification requirements.
(d) A U.S. person requesting a national interest exemption shall submit relevant information to the Department of the Treasury regarding the transaction and shall articulate the basis for the request, including the U.S. person's analysis of the transaction's potential impact on the national interest of the United States, and the certification set out in § 851.203. Information and other documents submitted by the U.S. person to the Department of the Treasury under this section shall be deemed part of the national interest exemption request. The U.S. person shall follow the instructions posted on the Department of the Treasury's Outbound Investment Security Program website. No communications or submissions other than those described in this section shall constitute a request for a national interest exemption. The Department of
(
printed page 67430)
the Treasury may request additional information that may include some or all of the information required under § 851.405.
(e) A determination that a covered national security transaction is exempt under this section may be subject to binding conditions.
(f) No determination pursuant to paragraph (a) of this section will be valid unless provided to the subject U.S. person in writing and signed by an official no less senior than Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Treasury for Investment Security.
Note 1 to § 851.502:
The process and related information for national interest exemption requests is available on the Department of the Treasury's Outbound Investment Security Program website.
§ 851.503
Intelligence activities exemption.
Transactions undertaken as part of any authorized intelligence activities of the United States shall not be regulated or prohibited, directly or indirectly, by this part.
Subpart F—Violations
§ 851.601
Taking actions prohibited by this part.
The taking of any action prohibited by this part is a violation of this part.
§ 851.602
Failure to fulfill requirements.
Failure to take any action required by this part, and within the time frame and in the manner specified by the regulations in this part, as applicable, is a violation of the regulations in this part.
§ 851.603
Misrepresentation, concealment, and omission of facts.
With respect to any information submission to or communication with the Department of the Treasury pursuant to any provision of this part, the making of any materially false or misleading representation, statement, or certification, or falsifying, concealing or omitting any material fact is a violation of this part.
§ 851.604
Evasions; attempts; causing violations; conspiracies.
(a) Any action that evades or avoids, has the purpose of evading or avoiding, causes a violation of, or attempts to violate any of the obligations set forth in this part is prohibited.
(b) Any conspiracy formed to violate the obligations set forth in this part is prohibited.
§ 851.605
Burden of proof.
In an enforcement action for a violation of this part, the burden of proof shall be upon the Secretary.
Subpart G—Penalties and Disclosures
§ 851.701
Penalties.
(a) Section 807 of Title VIII applies to any person subject to the jurisdiction of the United States who violates, attempts to violate, conspires to violate, or causes a violation of any order, regulation, or notification requirement, or prohibition under Title VIII.
(b) A civil penalty may be imposed on any person who violates, attempts to violate, conspires to violate, or causes a violation of any order, regulation, notification requirement, or prohibition issued under Title VIII, including any provision of this part in amounts equivalent to amounts provided for under section 206(b) of IEEPA. Those amounts are not to exceed the greater of:
(1) $250,000, as such amount is adjusted pursuant to the Federal Civil Penalties Inflation Adjustment Act of 1990, as amended (Pub. L. 101-410,
28 U.S.C. 2461 note
); or
(2) An amount that is twice the amount of the transaction that is the basis of the violation with respect to which the penalty is imposed.
(c) The civil penalties provided for in IEEPA are subject to adjustment pursuant to the Federal Civil Penalties Inflation Adjustment Act of 1990, as amended (Pub. L. 101-410,
28 U.S.C. 2461 note
). Notice of the maximum penalty which may be assessed under this section will be published in the
Federal Register
and on the Department of the Treasury's Outbound Investment Security Program website on an annual basis.
(d) The penalties available under this section are without prejudice to other penalties, civil or criminal, and forfeiture of property, available under other applicable law.
(e) Pursuant to
18 U.S.C. 1001
, whoever, in any matter within the jurisdiction of the executive, legislative, or judicial branch of the Government of the United States, knowingly and willfully falsifies, conceals or covers up by any trick, scheme, or device a material fact; makes any materially false, fictitious, or fraudulent statement or representation; or makes or uses any false writing or document knowing the same to contain any materially false, fictitious, or fraudulent statement or entry shall be fined under title 18, United States Code, or imprisoned not more than 5 years, or both.
§ 851.702
Administrative collection; referral to United States Department of Justice.
The imposition of a monetary penalty under this part creates an immediate debt due to the U.S. Government. The Department of the Treasury may take action to collect the penalty assessed if not paid. In addition or instead, the matter may be referred to the Department of Justice for appropriate action to recover the penalty.
§ 851.703
Divestment.
(a) The Secretary may compel the divestment of a covered national security transaction in a prohibited technology.
(b) The Secretary may refer any action taken under paragraph (a) of this section to the Attorney General to seek appropriate relief to enforce such action, including divestment or other relief.
§ 851.704
Voluntary self-disclosure.
(a) Any person that has engaged in conduct that may constitute a violation of this part may submit a voluntary self-disclosure of that conduct to the Department of the Treasury.
(b) In determining the appropriate response to any violation, the Department of the Treasury will consider the submission and the timeliness of any voluntary self-disclosure.
(c) In assessing the timeliness of a voluntary self-disclosure, the Department of the Treasury will consider whether it has learned of the conduct prior to the voluntary self-disclosure. The Department of the Treasury may consider disclosure of a violation to another government agency other than the Department of the Treasury as a voluntary self-disclosure based on a case-by-case assessment.
(d) Notwithstanding paragraphs (a) through (c) of this section, identification to the Department of the Treasury of conduct that may constitute a violation of this part may not be assessed to be a voluntary self-disclosure in one or more of the following circumstances:
(1) A different party has provided a prior disclosure to the Department of the Treasury of the conduct or similar conduct related to the same pattern or practice, regardless of whether the disclosing person knew of the different party's prior disclosure;
(2) The disclosure includes materially false or misleading information;
(3) The disclosure, when considered along with supplemental information timely provided by the disclosing person, is materially incomplete;
(4) The disclosure is not self-initiated, including when the disclosure results from a suggestion or order of a Federal or state agency or official;
(5) The disclosure is a response to an administrative subpoena or other inquiry from the Department of the Treasury or another government agency;
(
printed page 67431)
(6) The disclosure is made about the conduct of an entity by an individual in such entity without the authorization of such entity's senior management; or
(7) The filing is made pursuant to a required notification under this part, including § 851.403 or § 851.406.
(e) A voluntary self-disclosure to the Department of the Treasury must take the form of a written letter submitted through the electronic Outbound Notification System and addressed to the Assistant Secretary for Investment Security describing the conduct that may constitute a violation and each of the persons involved. Specifically, the letter must include, or be followed within a reasonable period by supplemental information that contains sufficient detail to afford a complete understanding of the conduct that may constitute the violation, including;
(1) Whether the relevant covered national security transaction (or transactions) was in a notifiable technology or prohibited technology, with reference to the relevant paragraph of § 851.218 or § 851.226;
(2) The date or dates on which the conduct occurred;
(3) The parties to the transaction(s);
(4) Whether any of the parties have established programs or protocols aimed at compliance with the regulations in this part;
(5) A description of any pre-transaction diligence undertaken by the U.S. person, including, as applicable, any steps described in § 851.104(c);
(6) A statement of the reason why the transaction was undertaken in light of the regulations in this part; and
(7) A proposal for mitigation of any harms associated with the violation, which may include divestment or a voluntary disgorgement of profits.
(f) A person making a voluntary self-disclosure must respond to any follow-up inquiries by the Department of the Treasury within the time frame and in the manner specified by the Department of the Treasury.
Subpart H—Provision and Handling of Information
§ 851.801
Confidentiality.
(a) Except to the extent required by law or otherwise provided in paragraph (b) of this section, any information or documentary materials not otherwise publicly available that are submitted to or filed with the Department of the Treasury under this part, including in connection with a compliance inquiry or action under subpart F of this part, shall be exempt from disclosure under
5 U.S.C. 552(b)(3)
, and no such material may be made public.
(b) Notwithstanding paragraph (a) of this section, except to the extent prohibited by law, the Department of the Treasury may disclose information or documentary materials that are not otherwise publicly available, subject to appropriate confidentiality and classification requirements, when such information is or documentary materials are:
(1) Relevant to any judicial or administrative action or proceeding;
(2) Provided to Congress or to any duly authorized committee or subcommittee of Congress;
(3) Important to the national security analysis or actions of the Secretary to any domestic governmental entity, or to any foreign governmental entity of a U.S. ally or partner, only to the extent necessary for national security purposes;
(4) The identity of a covered foreign person in any public database established under section 805 of Title VIII;
(5) Information that the submitting or filing parties have consented to be disclosed to non-parties; or
(6) Gathered by the Secretary or the Secretary's designee where the disclosure is determined by the Secretary or the Secretary's designee to be in the national interest, which may include publication of anonymized data.
§ 851.802
Language of information.
All materials or information submitted or filed with the Department of the Treasury under this part shall be submitted in English. If supplementary or additional materials were originally written in a foreign language, they shall be submitted in their original language. Where English versions of those documents exist, they shall also be submitted.
Subpart I—Non-Binding Feedback
§ 851.901
Eligibility to request feedback.
(a) This subpart establishes procedures by which an eligible person may request non-binding feedback from the Department of the Treasury as to whether a transaction would constitute a prohibited transaction under this part.
(b) Only a person with a direct financial interest in the subject transaction may submit a request under this subpart.
(c) The transaction that is the subject of the request must be an actual—not hypothetical—transaction and involve only prospective conduct (
i.e.,
conduct that has not yet occurred). An executed contract is not required, but the material terms of the prospective transaction must be identified in a binding written agreement or other binding document to demonstrate that the transaction is not hypothetical.
Note 1 to § 851.901:
Because feedback may only be requested for prospective conduct, submission of a voluntary self-disclosure under § 851.704 does not constitute a request under this subpart.
§ 851.902
Submission requirements.
(a) A request for non-binding feedback must be submitted in writing.
(b) A request must be submitted in accordance with the instructions found on the Department of the Treasury's Outbound Investment Security Program website or as otherwise specified by the Department of the Treasury.
(c) A request must address a single transaction.
(d) A request must include all relevant and material information bearing on whether the subject transaction would constitute a prohibited transaction, including:
(1) Identification of the requester and any other persons joining in the request, including name, address, place of incorporation or organization (if applicable), principal place of business, citizenship, and points of contact;
(2) Identification of each party to the transaction (including relevant intermediaries, financing sources, and controlled foreign entities), and each covered foreign person, if known;
(3) A detailed description of the contemplated structure of the transaction, including the form of investment, governance and information rights, timing, and completion date;
(4) A detailed description of the products, services, technologies, or activities implicated by the transaction and the basis for the requester's view as to whether such products, services, technologies, or activities may constitute prohibited technology;
(5) All operative documents and material term sheets, draft agreements, side letters, and other written materials reflecting the contemplated transaction, as available at the time of submission;
(6) Any other information that the requester believes is relevant to the application of this part to the transaction, including any prior submissions to the Department of the Treasury under this part or part 850 of this chapter concerning the same or closely related transaction, or any other information that may be material to the subject transaction; and
(7) A statement as to whether the requester seeks:
(i) Anonymized guidance to the public; or
(ii) Confidential non-binding feedback provided to the requester.
(
printed page 67432)
(e) A request must be signed by an authorized representative of the requester or by counsel expressly authorized in writing to sign on the requester's behalf and the signer must certify
(1) That the request contains a true, correct, and complete disclosure of all material facts and circumstances known to the requester at the time of submission; and
(2) That the requester will promptly supplement the request if the requester learns of material changes to facts stated in the request or omissions therefrom.
(f) A requester may identify in its submission any information that it considers proprietary or identifying to assist in the event anonymized guidance is issued to the public.
§ 851.903
Additional information; completeness.
(a) If a request does not contain all information the Department of the Treasury deems necessary to review the matter, the Department of the Treasury may request additional information or documents, or a meeting with the requester and any other relevant parties to the transaction.
(b) Failure to provide requested information within the time frame specified by the Department of the Treasury may result in the closing of the request without providing feedback.
(c) A request will not be deemed complete until the Department of the Treasury receives all additional information it has requested.
Note 1 to § 851.903:
The Department of the Treasury may request additional information from other relevant parties to conduct its analysis.
§ 851.904
Issuance of non-binding feedback.
(a) Receipt of a complete request for non-binding feedback by an eligible person under this subpart does not obligate the Department of the Treasury to issue such feedback.
(b) The Department of the Treasury may, in its sole discretion, respond to a complete request by providing anonymized public guidance, issuing confidential, written non-binding feedback stating the Department of the Treasury's view as to whether the transaction, as described, would constitute a covered national security transaction in a prohibited technology, or declining to provide feedback. When providing feedback, the Department of the Treasury may, in its sole discretion, respond to some, but not all, of the questions or information provided by the requestor (
e.g.,
non-binding feedback limited to whether the foreign person is a covered foreign person).
(c) No oral clearance, release, or other statement purporting to provide non-binding feedback under this subpart may be given.
(d) Non-binding feedback does not express the Department of the Treasury's views on any legal or factual issues that may arise under other statutes or regulations, or before any other department or agency.
(e) Non-binding feedback may be invalidated, modified, or revoked by the Department of the Treasury at any time, including if it was based on inaccurate, incomplete, or outdated information.
§ 851.905
Effect of non-binding feedback.
(a) Any non-binding feedback issued under this subpart is not binding on the Department of the Treasury, any other Federal or local department or agency, or any court; does not constitute an authorization, license, exemption, or waiver; and does not preclude the Department of the Treasury from taking any action authorized by law with respect to the transaction, the requester, or any other person.
(b) In determining an appropriate response to a potential violation under this part, the Department of the Treasury may consider, among other factors, whether the requester sought and reasonably acted consistent with non-binding feedback, provided that the requester made a true, correct, and complete disclosure of all material facts and circumstances known to the requester at the time of submission.
§ 851.906
Anonymized public guidance.
Anonymized public guidance issued pursuant to this subpart may take the form of answers to frequently asked questions, standalone regulatory guidance, or anonymized versions of the feedback provided to a requestor.
§ 851.907
Limitations; frivolous feedback requests.
(a) In establishing and administering processes under this subpart, the Department of the Treasury may reject or otherwise limit any request identified as frivolous. The Department of the Treasury may identify a request as frivolous in its sole discretion and based on a totality of the circumstances, including whether the request:
(1) Lacks sufficient detail or supporting materials to permit meaningful review;
(2) Duplicates, without material change, a prior request by the same requester;
(3) Seeks general advisory views or policy guidance not specific to the transaction described;
(4) Is submitted in bad faith, for purposes of delay, harassment, or to burden the Department of the Treasury; or
(5) Otherwise fails to further the administration or enforcement of this part.
(b) The Department of the Treasury, in its sole discretion, may place limitations on a requester that submits a frivolous request. Such limitations may include declining to accept the request, closing the request, requiring consolidation of multiple requests, limiting the number of requests submitted by a requester within a specified period, or requiring pre-submission consultation, as specified by the Department of the Treasury through public notice or instructions published on the Department of the Treasury's Outbound Investment Security Program website.
§ 851.908
Signature requirement.
Confidential non-binding feedback must be signed by the Assistant Secretary of the Treasury for Investment Security, a Deputy Assistant Secretary for Investment Security, or another official acting pursuant to § 851.1101 or other applicable delegation.
Subpart J—Information on Covered Foreign Persons
§ 851.1001
Confidential submission of information on covered foreign persons.
(a) Any person may submit information, including supporting documents, to the Department of the Treasury regarding whether a foreign person is a covered foreign person engaged in a prohibited technology or in a notifiable technology. Submission instructions are available on the Department of the Treasury's Outbound Investment Security Program website.
(b) A person submitting information must include their:
(1) Full legal name (last, first, middle name);
(2) Occupation or line of work, including name of employer (if any); and
(3) Contact information.
(c) The submission must include the following information, as applicable, and to the best of the submitter's ability, about the foreign person that is the subject of the confidential submission:
(1) Name, including any known aliases;
(2) Principal place(s) of business;
(3) Place of incorporation or legal organization;
(4) Company address(es);
(5) Company website;
(6) Any information regarding the foreign person's nationality (if an
(
printed page 67433)
individual) or ownership (if an entity), including the foreign person's ultimate owner, and the full legal names and titles of each officer, director, and other member of management of the foreign person;
(7) The notifiable technology or prohibited technology in which the foreign person is engaged by reference to the relevant paragraph under § 851.218 or § 851.226, as appropriate; and
(8) Any other information that the submitter believes would assist the Department of the Treasury to analyze and understand the information submitted.
(d) The submission must also include an explanation regarding how the submitter determined or discovered that the foreign person is engaged in a prohibited technology or a notifiable technology. (e) The Department of the Treasury may contact the submitter with follow-up inquiries regarding the submission.

Subpart K—Other Provisions
§ 851.1101
Delegation of authorities of the Secretary of the Treasury.
Any action that the Secretary is authorized to take pursuant to Title VIII may be taken by the Assistant Secretary of the Treasury for Investment Security or their designee or by any other person to whom the Secretary has delegated the authority so to act, as appropriate.
§ 851.1102
Amendment, modification, or revocation.
(a) Except as otherwise provided by law, the Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of Commerce, the Secretary of State, and, as appropriate, the heads of other relevant Federal departments and agencies, may amend, modify, or revoke provisions of this part at any time.
(b) Except as otherwise provided by law, any instructions, orders, forms, regulations, or rulings issued pursuant to this part may be amended, modified, or revoked at any time.
(c) Unless otherwise specifically provided, any amendment, modification, or revocation of any provision in this part does not affect any act done or omitted, or any civil or criminal proceeding commenced or pending, prior to such amendment, modification, or revocation. All penalties, forfeitures, and liabilities under any such instructions, orders, forms, regulations, or rulings pursuant to this part continue and may be enforced as if such amendment, modification, or revocation had not been made.
§ 851.1103
Severability.
The provisions of this part are separate and severable from one another. If any of the provisions of this part, or the application thereof to any person or circumstance, is held to be invalid, such invalidity shall not affect other provisions or application of such provisions to other persons or circumstances that can be given effect without the invalid provision or application.
§ 851.1104
Reports to be furnished on demand.
(a) Any person is required to furnish under oath, in the form of reports or otherwise, at any time as may be required by the Department of the Treasury, complete information regarding any act or transaction subject to the provisions of this part, regardless of whether such act or transaction is effected pursuant to a national interest exemption under § 851.502. Except as provided otherwise, the Department of the Treasury may, through any person or agency, conduct investigations, hold hearings, administer oaths, examine witnesses, receive evidence, take depositions, and require by subpoena the attendance and testimony of witnesses and the production of any books, contracts, letters, papers, and other hard copy or electronic documents relating to any matter under investigation, regardless of whether any report has been required or filed under this section.
(b) For purposes of paragraph (a) of this section, the term
document
includes any written, recorded, or graphic matter or other means of preserving thought or expression (including in electronic format), and all tangible things stored in any medium from which information can be processed, transcribed, or obtained directly or indirectly.
(c) Persons providing documents to the Department of the Treasury pursuant to this section must do so in a usable format agreed upon by the Department of the Treasury.

title: Certain Corrugated Die-Cut Cardboard Boxes From the People's Republic of China, Malaysia, and the Republic of Türkiye: Initiation of Less-Than-Fair-Value Investigations
dates: Applicable October 19, 2026.
full_text:
